title: Cap. 1 prol. IV: common vs distinguishing — Davenant denies foresight discriminators
pass_a_gloss: You see already a great discrimination between those prior conditions of the subject, which we have called common, and these later ones, which we name distinguishing. For rational nature, and nature subjected to sin, is presupposed in the predestined and reprobate subject, so that in them no cause, reason, or occasion of discrimination is placed; but good works and evil, faith and unbelief, are so placed as foresight conditions in humans that according to them the very discrimination of predestined or reprobate humans proceeds. Although therefore we concede the prior conditions as prerequisites, so that the subject commonly and promiscuously can lie under God predestining and reprobating, yet these later ones, which many strive to establish, we utterly deny to be presupposed and foreseen by God in the human to be predestined or reprobated, or that for their foresight diversity diverse acts of predestination and reprobation always tend unto diverse persons. Key lemmas: communes / distinguentes; discrimen; praesupponi; praevideri.
pass_b_english: You already see the great difference between those earlier subject-conditions we called common, and these later ones we call distinguishing. Rational nature, and nature under sin, is presupposed in the predestined and the reprobate so that nothing in them is set as cause, reason, or occasion of the divide. Good and evil works, faith and unbelief, are instead set as foresight conditions in people so that the very divide between the predestined and the reprobate proceeds according to them. We grant the earlier conditions as prerequisites — so that a subject can, commonly and without distinction, lie under God as he predestines and reprobates. But these later ones, which many try to fix in place, we flatly deny: they are not presupposed or foreseen by God in the person to be predestined or reprobated, nor do different foresight varieties of them always drive different acts of predestination and reprobation onto different persons.
source_text: Videtis jam magnum discrimen inter priores illas conditiones subjecti, quas communes appellavimus, & has posteriores, quas distinguentes nuncupamus. Nam natura Rationalis, & Peccato subdititia, praesupponitur in subjecto praedestinato & reprobato, ut in illis nulla ponatur causa, ratio, aut occasio discriminis; sed Bona opera & Mala, Fides & Infidelitas, ita ponuntur praevisae condiciones in hominibus, ut secundum illas procedat ipsum discrimen hominum praedestinatorum aut reprobatorum. Quanquam ergo concedamus priores conditiones praerequisitas, ut subjectum communiter & promiscue possit subjacere Deo praedestinanti & reprobanti, tamen hasce posteriores, quas multi stabilire conantur, prorsus pernegamus praesupponi & praevideri a Deo in homine praedestinando aut reprobando, aut pro earum diversitate praevisa diversos actus praedestinationis atque reprobationis tendere semper in diversas personas.
